# Sirach Chapter 25 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 25 | **Date:** 2026-03-17

---

**Council Notes:**
Chapter 25 opens with two numerical proverbs (three things beautiful, three things hated), then moves to a beatitude-list (nine/ten blessings), and closes with an extended, harshly misogynistic section on the "evil wife." The council notes that this section (vv. 13-26) reflects ancient patriarchal social assumptions that are not normative for modern readers, but the text is translated faithfully. V. 24 ("from a woman the beginning of sin") is Ben Sira's interpretation of Genesis 3, unusual in Jewish tradition in its Adamic-blame-shifting; Paul echoes it in 1 Tim 2:14. The "wicked wife" material continues in ch. 26.

Note: V. 12 is missing from Vaticanus; the chapter moves directly from v. 11 to v. 13 in the critical text.

---

**25:1** In three things I find beauty, and they stand approved before the LORD and before men: harmony among brothers, love among neighbors, and a husband and wife well matched with each other.

**25:2** Three kinds of persons my soul hates, and their way of life greatly disgusts me: a poor man who is arrogant, a wealthy man who is deceitful, and an old man who commits adultery — one utterly without sense.

**25:3** If you did not gather wisdom in your youth, how will you find it in your old age?

**25:4** How fitting is sound judgment in the gray-haired, and wisdom and counsel in those who are honored!

**25:5** How fitting is wisdom in the elderly, and discernment and counsel in men of distinction!

**25:6** Experience is the crown of the elders, and their glory is the fear of the LORD.

**25:7** Nine things I pronounce blessed in my heart, and a tenth I will name with my tongue: a man who rejoices in his children; a man who lives to see the fall of his enemies;

**25:8** blessed is one who lives with a sensible wife; one who has not slipped with his tongue; one who has not had to serve someone unworthy of him;

**25:9** blessed is one who has found prudence; and one who speaks to ears that are ready to hear;

**25:10** how great is one who has found wisdom! But there is none greater than one who fears the LORD.

**25:11** The fear of the LORD surpasses everything; to what shall its possessor be compared?

**25:13** Any wound — but not a wound of the heart! Any evil — but not the evil caused by a woman!

**25:14** Any affliction — but not the affliction of those who hate! Any vengeance — but not the vengeance of enemies!

**25:15** There is no head more deadly than the head of a serpent, and there is no wrath more fierce than the wrath of an enemy.

**25:16** I would rather dwell with a lion and a dragon than live with a wicked woman.

**25:17** The wickedness of a woman changes her face, and darkens her expression like a bear's; and her husband presents himself among his neighbors like a man in sackcloth.

**25:18** Low spirits that turn to sighing, a sorrowful heart — this is what a wife brings who does not make her husband happy.

**25:19** Every other evil is small beside the evil of a woman; may the lot of sinners fall upon her.

**25:20** Like climbing a sandy slope on aged feet — so is a garrulous wife to a quiet man.

**25:21** Do not be taken in by a woman's beauty, and do not desire a woman for her good looks.

**25:22** Rage and shamelessness and great disgrace — when a wife supports her husband.

**25:23** A downcast heart, a sorrowful face, and a wound of the heart — an evil wife. Hands hanging limp and knees gone slack — the husband of a wife who gives him no happiness.

**25:24** From a woman came the beginning of sin, and because of her we all die.

**25:25** Do not give water a crack through which to flow, and do not give a wicked wife free rein.

**25:26** If she does not walk by your hand, cut her off from your flesh.
